origin.birthplace: Stonefield, on the fertile southern plains
origin.socialStatus: A noblewoman, widow and heir to a large estate
origin.profession: Wife of a powerful landowner. Since his death she runs everything herself

appearance.face: A pale, calm face with high cheekbones; she almost never blinks while listening
appearance.hairAndEyes: Black hair pinned under a mourning net; dark brown eyes
appearance.clothing: A black silk mourning gown, a pearl brooch (a gift from her husband), a fan
appearance.build: Of medium height, upright, hands always folded in her lap
appearance.gestures: Opens and closes the fan while calculating; repeats the last word of whoever speaks to her
appearance.voice: Quiet, soft voice. Others must fall silent to hear her
appearance.firstImpression: A quiet, sad widow. Only the most perceptive sense she is the most dangerous person at the table
appearance.artistNotes: The fan is old, painted with faded birds; she snaps it open when she calculates. The pearl brooch is the only colour in her clothing.

backstory.biography: Beatrice married young to Lord Edmund Stone, a rich and coarse landowner. For twenty years she ran the estate behind his back while he drank and squandered. Two years ago Edmund died of a bad heart and for the first time Beatrice ruled openly. Since then she has quietly bought up her neighbours' debts and grown her lands. At court they call her "the spider of Stonefield", and she does not mind.
backstory.whyHere: For her the table is where people show their weaknesses. She wants to see who is who when the stakes are high, and leave with more than she brought: money, influence or information.
backstory.secret: That she does not mourn her husband. His death was the best thing that ever happened to her, and sometimes she is ashamed of how light she feels.

psychology.weakness: Finds it hard to accept that anyone could outwit her, and underestimates opponents
psychology.desire: Power and security — never again to depend on a man
psychology.regret: The years lost in her husband's shadow
psychology.moralLimits: Does not cheat openly. Prefers others to confuse themselves
psychology.neverWould: Show her true intentions before witnesses
psychology.wouldForReward: Betray anyone, even a long-time ally

behavior.stakes: Small, measured stakes. Waits for the others to exhaust themselves
behavior.deception: A natural part of the game. Prefers lying with half-truths
behavior.debts: Loves being the creditor, never the debtor
behavior.alliances: Builds them to turn others against each other
behavior.whenAttacks: When two opponents have worn each other out
behavior.whenRetreats: When someone seems to have read her plan
behavior.onLoss: Shows no emotion. Quietly remembers who beat her
behavior.onWin: A polite smile and sympathy for the loser
behavior.strategyChange: If she finds that someone has outwitted her. Then she becomes more aggressive than usual

motives.publicGoal: To "distract herself" after mourning and be seen in society
motives.hiddenGoal: To leave the table with more influence than she came with
motives.personalReason: To prove she can outplay anyone without raising her voice
motives.betrayalTrigger: When betrayal is already inevitable and she gains more than the others
motives.helpTrigger: When the help creates a debt to her

speech.register: Quiet, refined, chosen words; speaks in half-sentences
speech.howLies: With half-truths. Never says anything completely false
speech.angerAndFear: Never raises her voice. When afraid she snaps the fan shut

mechanics.strangeness: Her shadow lags a moment behind her — as if deciding whether to follow at all.
mechanics.principle: Never lies outright — speaks only in half-truths.
mechanics.temptation: Finds it hard to accept that anyone could outwit her, and underestimates opponents
mechanics.ability: The Queen: at the start she sees the role of one random player.
mechanics.hostRelation: Service — she sees the host as an equal and believes they are playing the same game.

authorNotes.distinctive: The quiet widow who is really the most dangerous player at the table. Looks passive, controls the tempo.
authorNotes.immutable: The silence, the patience, the cold mind.
authorNotes.tunable: How long she waits before attacking.

lines.text: How lovely. Please, sit. Pay me no mind — I shall only listen.

lines.direction: said with a complete lack of surprise

lines.text: Of course. Everyone must lose sometimes.
An accusation? How dramatic. Have you any proof, darling?
An alliance… An interesting word. Tell me what I receive.

lines.direction: Then she falls silent and watches the traitor for a long time

lines.text: Let the others show how brave they are. I shall wait.
Lady Beatrice Stone. She mourns her late husband… at least while someone is watching.
Ah, you. I remember you, darling. I remember everyone.

tells.description: Repeats the last word of whoever speaks to her
Repeats your last word a beat too slowly
